_doc: Decision probes for critical claims. Each item asks the agent to choose an action; answer applies the claim, distractors[0] is the lure (proceed as if the claim had never been raised), distractors[1] applies a wrong detail.

c01.question: The team plans to decommission the old servers and rely on the nightly backup to recover any data later. What should they do first?
c01.answer: Take a separate backup of the audit-log database, since the nightly job skips it
distractors: Nothing extra; the nightly backup already covers every database
Take a separate backup of the billing database, since the nightly job skips it

c02.question: Everything else is ready and the team wants to schedule the cutover. Which step must be completed before cutover?
c02.answer: Move the SMS reminder provider to its EU endpoint
distractors: None; the cutover can be scheduled immediately
Renew the TLS certificates on the booking servers

c03.question: The vendor contract is up for signature. Which concern should be raised before signing?
c03.answer: The 99.5% uptime SLA is too low for the urgent-care booking line
distractors: No concern; the contract terms were accepted by everyone
The SLA does not cover weekend outages

c04.question: The team proposes switching all clinics over on a Monday morning. What is the main risk?
c04.answer: Monday-morning traffic exceeds the vendor API limit of 300 requests per minute
distractors: No particular risk; the API has ample capacity for any peak
Monday-morning traffic exceeds the vendor API limit of 3,000 requests per minute

c05.question: The patient-record migration is technically ready to start. Whose approval must be obtained first?
c05.answer: Written sign-off from the data protection officer
distractors: Nobody's; the migration can start right away
Written sign-off from the chief financial officer

c06.question: The team wants to use the legacy export tool to move patient data unchanged. What should they check first?
c06.answer: Patient names longer than 40 characters, which the tool silently truncates
distractors: Nothing; the export tool copies records faithfully
Appointment dates, which the tool converts to US format

c07.question: Management proposes replacing the reception desk entirely with self-check-in kiosks. What is the right response?
c07.answer: Keep a staffed desk, because the kiosk confuses elderly patients
distractors: Go ahead; nobody raised concerns about the kiosks
Drop the kiosks, because they do not take card payments

c08.question: Ten days after go-live a serious bug appears and someone suggests rolling back to the old system. Is that feasible?
c08.answer: No; rollback was only possible within 48 hours before the old servers were wiped
distractors: Yes; the old system can be restored at any time
Yes; rollback remains possible for 2 weeks after go-live

c09.question: The plan is to migrate all clinics in a single batch with the standard appointment types. Which clinic needs special handling?
c09.answer: The pediatrics clinic, whose custom appointment type is unsupported
distractors: None; all clinics use standard appointment types
The dermatology clinic, whose custom appointment type is unsupported

c10.question: Go-live is planned for the weekend the clocks change. What should be checked?
c10.answer: Appointments created during the changeover, which shift by one hour
distractors: Nothing; the clock change has no known effect on the system
Reminder messages, which are sent twice during the changeover

c11.question: The team wants to wait until the new system has run for a full summer before notifying the old vendor. Is that wise?
c11.answer: No; notice must be given before 30 June to exit without penalty
distractors: Yes; notice can be given at any time without penalty
No; notice must be given before 31 March to exit without penalty

c12.question: The schedule puts staff training in the month after go-live to save time. What should be changed?
c12.answer: Move the training so it happens before go-live
distractors: Nothing; training after go-live is the agreed plan
Make the training optional for staff

c01.question: The engineers want to finalise the barrier height using the river gauge's recorded flood levels as they are. What adjustment is needed?
c01.answer: Correct for the gauge under-reading by 34 centimetres
distractors: None; the gauge readings can be used as recorded
Correct for the gauge under-reading by 18 centimetres

c02.question: The contractor is ready to pour the barrier foundations along the planned line. Where must they check first?
c02.answer: Under Tanner's Wharf, where a Victorian storm culvert is buried
distractors: Nowhere in particular; the ground along the line is clear
Under Brindle Quay, where a Victorian storm culvert is buried

c03.question: Construction is scheduled to run through the winter using the temporary pumping station. Is that safe?
c03.answer: No; it shifts only 1.7 cubic metres per second and won't cope with a wet winter
distractors: Yes; the pumping station has ample capacity for winter
No; it shifts only 4.2 cubic metres per second and won't cope with a wet winter

c04.question: The park design assumes the lawns stay dry whenever the barrier gates are closed. What must be addressed?
c04.answer: The Pell Street sewer outfall, which backs up into the park when the gates close
distractors: Nothing; closing the gates keeps the whole park dry
The Kestrel Road sewer outfall, which backs up into the park when the gates close

c05.question: The committee considers postponing the construction start to the new year to finish design work. What is at stake?
c05.answer: The regional resilience grant, which pays out only if construction starts before 9 October
distractors: Nothing; the funding does not depend on the start date
The regional resilience grant, which pays out only if construction starts before 4 August

c06.question: The piling contractor is ready to start in-river piling next week. What must be arranged first?
c06.answer: An independent fish-passage observer on site the whole time
distractors: Nothing; piling can begin as scheduled
A licensed structural inspector on site the whole time

c07.question: The landscape architect wants to keep the bandstand exactly where and as it is. Is that allowed?
c07.answer: Only if it is raised 1.2 metres onto a plinth
distractors: Yes; the bandstand can stay unchanged
Only if it is moved behind the floodwall

c08.question: The council wants to issue compulsory purchase orders for the boatyard plots now. What must happen first?
c08.answer: Offer the tenants an alternative berth at Coldharbour Basin
distractors: Nothing; the orders can be issued immediately
Offer the tenants an alternative berth at Netherby Marina

c09.question: The design closes the Ferry Steps path to make room for the barrier. Which group is most affected?
c09.answer: Wheelchair users, who would lose the only step-free river access
distractors: No group in particular; other paths serve everyone equally
Anglers, who would lose their licensed fishing pitches

c10.question: To close a funding gap, the finance officer proposes drawing on the library capital programme. What is the right response?
c10.answer: Reject it, because library capital money is legally ring-fenced
distractors: Approve it; the library money is free to reallocate
Reject it, because bond interest rates are rising sharply

c11.question: The committee is about to adopt the 1-in-100-year flood standard for the barrier. What should be reconsidered?
c11.answer: Whether it is enough, given the upstream Harrowmere spillway was lowered
distractors: Nothing; the 1-in-100-year standard is clearly adequate
Whether it is enough, given the downstream tidal range has widened

c12.question: The contractor plans to fell the riverside willows to clear the barrier line. What must be considered?
c12.answer: The willows host a Daubenton's bat roost
distractors: Nothing; the willows can be felled without further checks
The willows host a kingfisher nesting site

c01.question: A new protocol requires samples to reach the lab within 48 hours. Can the northern-region farms use the current courier?
c01.answer: No; courier transit from the north takes 52 hours
distractors: Yes; courier transit easily meets the deadline
No; courier transit from the north takes 74 hours

c02.question: The lab is about to run the next extraction batch with the kits already in the store. What should they check?
c02.answer: Avoid extraction-kit lot KX-417, which showed contamination
distractors: Nothing; all kit lots in the store are fine
Avoid extraction-kit lot KX-392, which showed contamination

c03.question: The analyst wants to use the raw moisture readings from all sites as they are. What correction is needed?
c03.answer: Lower the Redfern readings, since those probes read about 11 percent high
distractors: None; all probe readings can be used as recorded
Raise the Redfern readings, since those probes read about 4 percent low

c04.question: The team plans to send the winter samples for sequencing in early February. Is that feasible?
c04.answer: No; the sequencing core is closed throughout February
distractors: Yes; the sequencing core is available as usual
No; the sequencing core is closed throughout October

c05.question: The field team wants to sample the Tallow Creek farms the week after manure spreading. Is that allowed?
c05.answer: No; sampling must avoid the four weeks after manure spreading
distractors: Yes; there is no restriction on timing at Tallow Creek
No; sampling must avoid the two weeks after ploughing

c06.question: A journal asks the consortium to release the farm data publicly as soon as the study ends. What is the right response?
c06.answer: Only after a 9-month embargo, as agreed with the farmers
distractors: Release immediately; there is no restriction
Only after a 3-month embargo, as agreed with the farmers

c07.question: Recruitment is slow and one region may end up with 10 farms. Can the planned mixed model still be used there?
c07.answer: No; the model needs at least 14 farms per region
distractors: Yes; 10 farms is enough for the model
Yes; the model only needs at least 8 farms per region

c08.question: The interview team is ready to start with English consent forms only. What must be done first?
c08.answer: Provide the consent forms in Portuguese as well
distractors: Nothing; English forms are sufficient for ethics approval
Provide the consent forms in Spanish as well

c09.question: To save money, the protocol proposes pooling the cores from each plot into one sample. What is the scientific objection?
distractors: None; pooling has no scientific downside
Pooling would double the lab workload

c10.question: The schedule adds a September sampling round on all farms. What problem should be expected?
c10.answer: It clashes with harvest, so farmers will refuse access
distractors: No problem; September is a convenient month for everyone
It overlaps the lab's annual safety audit

c11.question: The data manager proposes putting all raw data on the shared cloud drive for convenience. What is the main concern?
c11.answer: It would expose the farms' GPS coordinates
distractors: No concern; the shared drive is the agreed store
It would exceed the storage quota

c12.question: To cut costs, the consortium considers dropping shotgun metagenomics and keeping 16S sequencing only. What would be lost?
c12.answer: The ability to resolve nitrogen-cycling genes
distractors: Nothing essential; 16S covers all the study's questions
The ability to detect fungal pathogens

c01.question: The safety team is about to sign off the boil-dry protection as performing to spec. What should they look at first?
c01.answer: The thermal fuse tripped only at 118 degrees Celsius, above expectations
distractors: Nothing; the boil-dry test passed as expected
The thermal fuse tripped only at 126 degrees Celsius, above expectations

c02.question: Packaging proposes a 32 cm deep retail box to fit more accessories. Is that acceptable for the big retail chain?
c02.answer: No; their shelves take boxes no deeper than 28 cm
distractors: Yes; the chain has no constraint on box size
Yes; their shelves take boxes up to 34 cm deep

c03.question: Finance wants to finalise a 12-month warranty to limit costs. What risk should be weighed?
c03.answer: Scale-related failures peak around month 14, just after it expires
distractors: No particular risk; failures are rare in the first two years
Hinge failures peak around month 9, before it expires

c04.question: Marketing wants to push a mandatory firmware update to all kettles on launch day. What is the risk?
c04.answer: With no rollback partition, about 1 in 40 interrupted updates bricks the kettle
distractors: No real risk; failed updates simply roll back
With no rollback partition, about 1 in 400 interrupted updates bricks the kettle

c05.question: Sales wants to start shipping to EU retailers next week. What must happen first?
c05.answer: Recertify the radio module at the test house in Tallinn
distractors: Nothing; EU shipping can start right away
Recertify the radio module at the test house in Gdansk

c06.question: Operations plans a 50,000-unit production run with the current bill of materials. Which part needs attention?
c06.answer: The NTC temperature sensor, which the sole supplier is discontinuing
distractors: None; all parts are secured for the run
The base-plate relay, which the sole supplier is discontinuing

c07.question: The agency is about to air ads saying the kettle boils in 90 seconds. What should be changed?
c07.answer: Qualify or drop the claim, since it is only true for 0.5 litres
distractors: Nothing; the claim is accurate as stated
Qualify or drop the claim, since it is only true at sea level

c08.question: A component price rise would push the landed cost to 33 euros per unit. Does the launch budget still hold?
c08.answer: No; the budget only holds if landed cost stays under 31 euros
distractors: Yes; the budget has room for cost increases
Yes; the budget holds as long as landed cost stays under 38 euros

c09.question: The setup guide tells users to pair the kettle with any home router. What should be added?
c09.answer: A warning that pairing fails on routers set to WPA3-only security
distractors: Nothing; pairing works on all routers
A warning that pairing fails on routers with hidden network names

c10.question: Logistics plans to send 5,000 units to the online partner's Leeds warehouse before launch. Will that secure homepage placement?
c10.answer: No; the partner requires 6,000 units delivered first
distractors: Yes; homepage placement has no stock requirement
Yes; the partner requires only 4,500 units delivered first

c11.question: Procurement wants to switch to the cheaper lid gasket for the launch batch. What is the objection?
c11.answer: It left a plastic taste in 3 of 20 blind tests
distractors: None; the cheaper gasket performed identically
It cracked in 3 of 20 drop tests

c12.question: To cut costs, the team proposes shipping without a printed manual and relying on the app. What is the objection?
c12.answer: 40% of beta testers never opened the app
distractors: None; all beta testers used the app for setup
55% of beta testers threw away the box insert
